note: Provenance for every figure under docs/_static/figures. One row per committed image. `sha256`, `bytes` and `used_in` are recomputed by `python tools/update_figure_manifest.py`; everything else is authored. `tests/test_figure_provenance.py` fails when a figure changes without its row, when a row names a generator or input that does not exist, or when a figure is added or removed without updating this file. Two fields are deliberately honest. `reproducible` says what it takes to rebuild the figure: `command` means the listed command rebuilds it from the repository alone, `manual` means a script produces the pixels but a rename, crop or format conversion is done by hand, and `external-data` means it also needs data that is not in the tree. `bytes_verified` says whether the committed bytes were actually re-derived and compared, which is a stronger claim: a `command` figure with `bytes_verified` false can be rebuilt, but its committed pixels predate the current renderer.

No docs page currently embeds it — it is kept as a generated asset for the objectives pages, and the empty used_in below records that honestly.

The bar heights are measurements from 2026-07-12 typed into the generator, not read from a committed artifact; re-running redraws the same typed numbers. Treat it as an illustration of the gradient-stack argument, not as a citable timing record. The `generated` date is the render, not the measurement.
